Passed 2026-06-02. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

The act requires the Connecticut Department of Economic and Community Development to develop a plan for an artificial intelligence small business program. The program would provide financial assistance to eligible small businesses to adopt and deploy artificial intelligence and establish a competitive small business environment for artificial intelligence technologies. The department must report the plan and any legislative recommendations to the General Assembly's commerce committee by January 1, 2027.

Who it applies to

  • Department of Economic and Community Development

Effective date

Effective from passage (Sec. 1)

Key definitions

  • artificial intelligence: a machine-based system that makes predictions, recommendations or decisions influencing real or virtual environments (Sec. 1(a)(1))
  • artificial intelligence technology: a computer system, application or other product that uses or incorporates one or more forms of artificial intelligence (Sec. 1(a)(2))
  • financial assistance: any and all forms of grants, extensions of credit, loans or loan guarantees, equity investments or other forms of financing (Sec. 1(a)(3))

Obligations

  • Consult with other relevant state agencies, public institutions of higher education or any other public entity that the Department of Economic and Community Development deems necessary (Sec. 1(b))
  • Develop a plan to establish an artificial intelligence small business program for the purpose of providing financial assistance to eligible small businesses to adopt and deploy artificial intelligence and establishing a competitive small business environment for the development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies (Sec. 1(b))
  • Include in the plan eligibility criteria and an application process with guidelines and terms for financial assistance (Sec. 1(b))
  • Include in the plan a requirement that, as a condition of receiving financial assistance, any applicant train such applicant's employees to work with artificial intelligence and prepare any such employees whose jobs may be displaced as a result of the adoption of artificial intelligence for new roles with the applicant (Sec. 1(b))
  • Report on the plan, including any recommendations for legislative action required to implement the plan, to the joint standing committee of the General Assembly having cognizance of matters relating to commerce not later than January 1, 2027, in accordance with section 11-4a of the general statutes (Sec. 1(c))

Prohibitions

  • not stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

The act does not specify penalties, enforcement authority, or a private right of action. It requires a report to the joint standing committee on commerce by January 1, 2027 (Sec. 1(c)).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying artificial intelligence is not directly regulated by this act, but if the planned program is implemented, small businesses seeking financial assistance to adopt and deploy artificial intelligence would need to meet eligibility criteria and application guidelines and would be required to train employees to work with artificial intelligence and prepare employees whose jobs may be displaced for new roles (Sec. 1(b)).
  • The act requires the Department of Economic and Community Development to develop a plan that may lead to future legislative action, so the terms of any eventual program could affect how small businesses deploy artificial intelligence (Sec. 1(c)).

Notable exemptions

  • not stated in the text

Compliance steps

  • Consult with other relevant state agencies, public institutions of higher education or other public entities deemed necessary (Sec. 1(b)).
  • Develop a plan to establish an artificial intelligence small business program with the stated purposes (Sec. 1(b)).
  • Include eligibility criteria and an application process with guidelines and terms for financial assistance in the plan (Sec. 1(b)).
  • Include the employee training and job displacement preparation requirement as a condition of receiving financial assistance in the plan (Sec. 1(b)).
  • Report on the plan and any recommendations for legislative action to the joint standing committee on commerce by January 1, 2027, in accordance with section 11-4a of the general statutes (Sec. 1(c)).

Senate Bill No. 417

 Special Act No. 26-23


AN ACT REQUIRING THE DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AND
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT TO DEVELOP A PLAN TO
ESTABLISH AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SMALL BUSINESS
PROGRAM.


Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives in General
Assembly convened:

 Section 1. (Effective from passage) (a) As used in this section, (1)
"artificial intelligence" means a machine-based system that makes
predictions, recommendations or decisions influencing real or virtual
environments, (2) "artificial intelligence technology" means a computer
system, application or other product that uses or incorporates one or
more forms of artificial intelligence, and (3) "financial assistance" means
any and all forms of grants, extensions of credit, loans or loan
guarantees, equity investments or other forms of financing.

 (b) The Department of Economic and Community Development, in
consultation with other relevant state agencies, public institutions of
higher education or any other public entity that the Department of
Economic and Community Development deems necessary, shall
develop a plan to establish an artificial intelligence small business
program for the purpose of (1) providing financial assistance to eligible
small businesses to adopt and deploy artificial intelligence to achieve
improvements in productivity and the quality of any products or
  Senate Bill No. 417
services offered by such small businesses, and (2) establishing a
competitive small business environment for the development and
deployment of artificial intelligence technologies. Such plan shall
include, but need not be limited to, eligibility criteria and an application
process with guidelines and terms for financial assistance for the
program, and a requirement that, as a condition of receiving financial
assistance, any applicant train such applicant's employees to work with
artificial intelligence and prepare any such employees, whose jobs may
be displaced as a result of the adoption of artificial intelligence, for new
roles with the applicant.

 (c) Not later than January 1, 2027, the Department of Economic and
Community Development shall report on such plan, including any
recommendations for legislative action required to implement such
plan, in accordance with the provisions of section 11-4a of the general
statutes, to the joint standing committee of the General Assembly
having cognizance of matters relating to commerce.
